data.title: U.S. Spot SOL ETFs Record $1.40M Net Outflow, Grayscale GSOL Leads With $1.11M
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing RootData, U.S. spot SOL ETFs recorded a combined net outflow of $1.40 million on November 19 (U.S. Eastern Time). Grayscale’s GSOL led with $1.11 million in outflows; its cumulative net inflows stood at $118 million as of that trading day. Invesco Galaxy’s QSOL saw $293,400 in net outflows, with cumulative net inflows of $2.62 million. Spot SOL ETFs’ total historical net inflows reached $1.42 billion.

data.title: Honda Unveils Asia Hybrid SUV as It Shifts From Failed EV Bet
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Honda Motor Co. unveiled a new flagship gas-electric hybrid SUV for Asia, the first in a range of hybrid models it plans to roll out this decade as it shifts away from fully electric cars.

data.title: Solidity Releases Version 0.8.39 to Fix Silent Storage-Corruption Vulnerability
data.description: According to ChainCatcher, Solidity has released version 0.8.39 to fix a medium-severity vulnerability that could silently corrupt storage without triggering an error. The bug affected multiple 0.8 versions and occurred when a recursive struct in storage was copied into a storage struct containing it. The fix adds a runtime overlap check, which increases gas consumption. The team said its scan of verified contracts found no affected deployed contracts.

data.title: AI | Copper Falls to Lowest Since March as Selloff Rattles Metals Markets
data.description: According to Bloomberg, copper fell to its lowest level since March after a week of market turmoil fueled by deepening concerns about global demand.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Anthropic’s Australia Data Center Project Faces Overwhelming Local Opposition
data.description: According to Jin10, project filings show that a planned data center in a remote area of Australia, with Anthropic (ANT.O) as its primary tenant, has faced overwhelming opposition from local residents. The proposed Western Downs Digital Park is about 250 kilometers west of Brisbane. Of nearly 600 public submissions, only two supported the project and one was neutral; the other 595 opposed it or called for delays until the developer addressed specific environmental concerns. The site is in farmland, far from suburban residential areas, and its planned computing load of 1.44 gigawatts would make it one of Australia’s largest data centers. About one-third of the submissions came from people living within 200 kilometers of the site. Opponents raised concerns about water use, electricity demand and prices, noise, road damage from construction vehicles, and pressure on housing supply.

data.title: Hong Kong Stocks Slide 20% From 2026 Peak as AI Selloff Widens
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Hong Kong stocks were heading for a bear market after falling 20% from their 2026 high, pressured by concerns about China’s economic health, the unraveling AI trade and US restrictions on chip exports.

data.title: Michael Burry Says He Warned on AI Stocks NVIDIA and CoreWeave
data.description:
Michael Burry said he had warned investors about NVIDIA, CoreWeave and Nebius, but had not told anyone to short them; all three stocks fell Thursday. Nebius dropped 9.4%, CoreWeave 6.1% and Nvidia 3.3%, according to BeInCrypto. Burry, a former Scion Asset Management fund manager, wrote on X Thursday that he had provided information investors could use to sell. TipRanks reported he holds Nvidia put options with a $140 strike expiring in February 2027. In a Nov. 12 Substack post, he said he doubled his Nasdaq-100 puts and rebuilt part of his position in the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH), which counts Nvidia among its top holdings. His Nasdaq-100 puts run into early 2027.

CoreWeave and Nebius sell AI developers access to Nvidia-powered servers. Burry argued that the two neoclouds, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and ASML relied on Nvidia’s market power. Nvidia shares have fallen 19% since Nov. 8, when co-founder Jensen Huang admitted extramarital affairs to staff; he resigned as CEO four days later. The company’s first post-Huang earnings report showed revenue up 103% to $115.8 billion. Interim CEO Colette Kress rejected concerns about neoclouds, saying the largest cloud operators were not pulling back. Nvidia closed at $145.98 Thursday, 39% below its October high. Burry became known for betting against the 2008 housing bubble.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Mistral Plans Singapore Regional Hub, Aims to Double Its Asia Workforce
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, French AI startup Mistral has established its Asia-Pacific headquarters in Singapore to meet growing regional demand for sovereign AI capabilities. The company plans to more than double its Asia-Pacific workforce to 200 by 2027, hiring in science, engineering, AI applications and robotics.

Mistral said the investment will support its goal of accelerating the development, training and real-world deployment of sovereign AI models. Co-founder and CEO Arthur Mensch said the company aims to make Singapore a strategic hub that enables governments and businesses across Asia-Pacific to control their infrastructure and intellectual assets and turn them into lasting economic value and industrial competitiveness.

In September, Mistral completed a funding round led by South Korea’s Samsung Electronics, valuing the company at more than $24 billion. The funding will support model development and customer-base expansion.

data.title: Bitcoin Slips Below $62,000 as Rate Hike Fears and Anthropic Debut Draw Risk Capital Away
data.description: Bitcoin fell below $62,000 on Friday, as a fresh round of hawkish Fed commentary and the largest AI listing to date pulled capital out of risk assets. U.S. equities fell to intraday lows at the same time Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq.Fed officials keep option of larger rate hike openChicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said he would consider all options at next month's meeting and did not rule out a larger-than-usual increase, according to Sina Finance. Inflation has stayed worryingly high for several months, he said, with little progress in the areas policymakers expected to improve. The Fed raised rates in September and held in October; since then, concern about reacceleration has grown and some officials have called for faster action.Stocks fall as Anthropic opens high after debutThe Dow dropped 1,101.11 points, or 2.19%, to 49,097.06, its first close below 50,000 since June. The S&P 500 lost 2.02% to 7,175.83 and the Nasdaq 2.25% to 23,879.20.Anthropic opened at $111.50, a 34% jump from its $83 IPO price, which was already set above the expected range. It pulled back about 13% from the opening high and closed up 17%. Bogart Wealth CIO Aleks Spencer called the listing a key test for the sector, saying Anthropic could become a new benchmark for AI sentiment after Nvidia's turmoil.

data.title: Aolani Cloud CEO Says Chip Restrictions May Have Halved Emerging Providers’ Valuations
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Bloomberg, Aolani Cloud Pte CEO Nicholas Chia said U.S. chip export restrictions on some markets may have cut valuations of Aolani and other emerging cloud providers in half. The United States has tightened chip supplies to parts of Southeast Asia, where several emerging cloud providers operate.

Chia said Aolani is considering contingency plans including moving its headquarters to the United States, seeking private credit financing, or being acquired by a larger emerging cloud provider. Weeks ago, Aolani received a financing letter of intent valuing it at $3 billion, compared with a $400 million valuation earlier this year. The company has also signed letters of intent to build data centers in several Asian locations.

data.title: Arthur Hayes Says ANT IPO Market Reaction Is Poor, Exits at a Loss
data.description: Arthur Hayes said on X that the market had reacted poorly to ANT’s IPO and that he had exited at a loss. According to Odaily, he will wait for a better time to go long again and said the Four Horsemen have now been decapitated.

data.title: BTCS Reports $54 Million in Aave Debt and $111 Million in Crypto Assets
data.description:
Ethereum treasury company BTCS said it borrowed stablecoins on Aave using some of its ETH as collateral as part of its ordinary operations. According to Foresight News, the funds are primarily used to finance liquidity pool positions operated through its DeFi business, Imperium.

BTCS said the position is actively managed and can change: it may borrow more if the value of its ETH collateral rises and reduce borrowing if the value falls.

As of November 19, 2026, BTCS had about $54 million in Aave debt and approximately $18 million in outstanding principal on senior secured convertible notes. Its crypto holdings were valued at about $111 million, based on an ETH price of $1,775 that day.

The company said it cannot predict ETH price movements or guarantee future borrowing amounts, collateral values, or that liquidation will not occur.

data.title: European Smartphone Shipments Fall 18%, Hit Lowest Quarterly Level in 13 Years
data.description: According to Jin10, European smartphone shipments fell 18% year over year in the third quarter, reaching their lowest quarterly level in 13 years. Counterpoint Research's third-quarter 2026 smartphone market monitor report, released on the 20th, attributed the market's sharp contraction to higher component costs that raised retail prices, fewer promotional campaigns, and macroeconomic uncertainty that curbed consumer spending. Samsung Electronics ranked first with a 35% market share, up 5 percentage points from 30% a year earlier. Apple ranked second, with its share rising 4 percentage points from 27% to 31%.

data.title: Address's MSTR and CRCL Long Positions Fully Liquidated Within Five Days, Losing $1.9 Million and $1.54 Million
data.description: According to Odaily, citing Lookonchain, an address’s 51,707-share MSTR long position, valued at $5 million, was fully liquidated five days ago, resulting in a $1.9 million loss. Four hours ago, its 33,246-share CRCL long position, valued at $1.69 million, was also fully liquidated, with a $1.54 million loss.

data.title: U.S. Floats Ukraine Ceding Territory to Russia for NATO Membership
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing The Wall Street Journal, the United States raised the possibility of Ukraine joining NATO in recent talks, including a proposal under which Ukraine would cede territory to Russia in exchange for membership.

data.title: EigenLayer Introduces Darkbloom Decentralized Compute Network and Yukon Research Platform
data.description:
EigenLayer has introduced Darkbloom, a decentralized compute network, and Yukon, a collaborative automated research platform. According to PANews, Eigen Labs Chief Growth Officer JT Rose announced the products on November 20.

Darkbloom lets device owners contribute unused computing capacity and earn revenue. Developers can use the network for private, low-cost inference to optimize open-source models. The network has handled paid inference requests and processed more than 1 trillion tokens in closed research testing.

Yukon enables people and AI agents to explore specific questions in parallel, with verified improvements shared across the network. Rose said that as Darkbloom’s core functions become protocolized and it begins charging platform fees, the protocol could direct those fees to the EIGEN token to convey value to the token.

data.title: Sky Says PSM-Linked Activity in Illegal-Activity Report Was Under 0.03% of Cumulative Volume
data.description:
Sky said activity cited in a CoinDesk report about illegal activity involving its Peg Stability Module (PSM) took place mainly through third-party permissionless platforms. According to Odaily, the PSM has processed more than $968 billion in transactions since launch, while the transactions cited in the report accounted for about 0.03% of that total.

Sky described the PSM as open on-chain infrastructure that supports the USDS and DAI stablecoin pegs through 1:1 exchanges. Its ecosystem frontends, including Spark, Grove, SkyMoney and Osero, screen and block flagged wallets to prevent users in sanctioned regions from accessing their services.

Sky founder Rune Christensen previously said the protocol was operating normally and had a sound financial position.

data.title: AMD Says It Follows U.S. Export Controls and Maintains Strict Compliance Processes Amid China Business Scrutiny
data.description:
An AMD spokesperson told Reuters in an emailed statement that allegations about the company’s business practices and partnerships were misrepresented. According to Odaily, Hunterbrook Media, a media outlet owned by short-selling firm Hunterbrook Capital, published an investigation on November 20 questioning AMD’s business ties with Chinese entities. The report said some related companies were linked to firms blacklisted by the U.S., potentially exposing AMD to closer regulatory scrutiny.

AMD said it complies with applicable U.S. export control laws and regulations and has established strict compliance processes across its global operations. The company said it would continue serving customers and uphold high standards of integrity.

data.title: Frasers CFO Demands Accent Group Chairman Quit During Australian Bid
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Frasers Group Plc’s pursuit of Australian retailer Accent Group Ltd. turned personal when Frasers’ finance chief flew to Accent’s annual meeting in Melbourne, publicly accused the company of underperformance and demanded that its chairman resign.

data.title: South Korea’s Base Group Considers $150 Million Investment in Trump-Linked Robotics Firm Foundation
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing Reuters, South Korean conglomerate Base Group is preparing to invest $150 million in Foundation Future Industries, a U.S. military robotics manufacturer backed by Eric Trump, son of U.S. President Donald Trump. Foundation has hired Eric Trump as chief strategy adviser.

Internal emails reviewed by Reuters show Foundation stopped paying employee salaries in recent weeks and is counting on funding from Base Group. A Base Group spokesperson confirmed the company is considering an investment, citing the long-term value of humanoid robots. Headquartered in Seoul, Base Group has drawn attention from the U.S. Congress over its ties to the Trump family.
